claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 16 and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can see you're asking about your son Alex who is 16 and lives at home with you.

Since Alex is 16, his eligibility depends on whether he's in approved education or training. **Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (This includes things like A-levels, Scottish Highers, NVQs, or other approved courses.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He left school and hasn't started anything yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Since Alex has left education and isn't in training, I need to ask:

**Has Alex registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services?** 

(If he has, you may still be able to get Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks after he left education or training.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with any careers service or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I have a few more questions to ensure I have a complete picture:

**Has Alex started any paid work? And if so, is he working 24 hours or more per week?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One final question to complete my assessment:

**Is Alex claiming any benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not claiming any benefits himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for answering all my questions. Based on the information you've provided, I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

Child Benefit normally continues for children aged 16 and over only if they stay in approved education or training (up to age 20). Since Alex has left school and is not currently in any approved education or training, he doesn't meet this requirement.

There is a provision that allows Child Benefit to continue for up to 20 weeks after a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training, but only if they register with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services. As Alex hasn't registered with either of these, this exception doesn't apply.

**However, please note:** If Alex does register with a careers service or enters approved education or training in the future, you may become eligible again. I'd recommend encouraging Alex to register with a careers service if he needs support finding work or training opportunities, as this could restore your Child Benefit eligibility for up to 20 weeks.
